doc: SignedSpawn v1 golden vectors, regenerated by `cargo test -p tmgr-spawn-auth -- --ignored regenerate`. All keys are TEST-ONLY (test_* fields). Secrets are 32 bytes of one repeated byte; P-256; public keys are 65-byte uncompressed SEC1 (0x04 prefix, on the curve; compressed or other lengths are refused), base64 STANDARD padded. Signatures are DER ECDSA P-256 over SHA-256 of the UTF-8 message, base64 STANDARD padded and canonical (re-encoding must reproduce the string); raw r||s, base64url and unpadded forms are refused. A verifier must accept high-S. CAPS: a signature string longer than 96 chars is refused as bad_sig and a key statement longer than 512 bytes as bad_token; these are DoS caps checked before any decoding (a valid DER signature is at most 96 chars and a valid statement is under 400 bytes, so no honest input reaches them); the over-cap cases use well-formed base64 / a correctly signed statement so only the cap can reject them. JSON READING (TypeScript port): parse the raw text with a strict JSON reader, not JSON.parse. Every number token must match ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ and then pass Number.isSafeInteger (so no '.', exponent, sign, -0, leading zero or value above 2^53-1); `v` must be a canonical integer; duplicate keys and unknown fields are refused; missing fields are refused. The phone hashes the `req` bytes exactly as received from the machine (never re-serialized) and compares with the proposal it displays. PROPOSAL: `proposal.fields` serialize to `proposal.canonical_utf8` in exactly the declared field order, no spaces, None omitted, serde_json escaping (quote, backslash, and control chars below U+0020 are escaped: \b \t \n \f \r short forms, others as lowercase \u00xx; '/', DEL, C1, U+2028 and all non-ASCII stay raw UTF-8); `req_sha256` is lowercase hex SHA-256 of those bytes; `canonical_cases[]` pins this escaping and `validate` says whether SpawnProposal::validate accepts the fields (cwd/name/task must be non-empty and contain no refused code point; cwd <= 4096 bytes, name/task <= 128 bytes; profile a token; prompt_sha256 64 lowercase hex; target_id mx_ + lowercase hex; v == 1; sandbox is absent or exactly the string "off", on a spawn only; it serializes right after mode and only when present). `proposal_json_cases[]` are raw proposal JSON texts: a `sandbox` that is not a string (true, 1) must be refused by the parser (`refused`), exactly "off" parses (`ok`). REFUSED CODE POINTS in cwd, name and task (one explicit table, inclusive ranges): all Cc (U+0000-001F, U+007F-009F), U+00AD, U+034F, U+061C, U+115F, U+1160, U+180E, U+200B-200F, U+2028-202E, U+2060-2064, U+2066-2069, U+206A-206F, U+3164, U+FE00-FE0F, U+FEFF, U+FFA0, U+FFF9-FFFB, U+E0000-E007F. Everything else is accepted (Cyrillic, astral emoji, U+2065, U+00AE and so on). U+200D (ZWJ) is refused, so ZWJ emoji sequences are refused; emoji without ZWJ and without U+FE0F are accepted. A port must iterate Unicode scalar values (code points), not UTF-16 units. `signed.message` is the exact signed string. VERIFY: `verify_cases[]`: given record (the machine's stored challenge, with its proposal; req_sha256 is recomputed from the proposal, never stored), pinned_key, wire (the SignedSpawn JSON), now_ms and the trust view (`trust` is the status the lookup returns for the device: trusted, not_trusted, revoked or unknown; a device is trusted only when trust is `trusted` and pinned_key.device_id == trusted_device_id, otherwise the status is not_trusted; a failed lookup must be reported as unknown; only trusted is accepted and everything else is refused as not_trusted), verify must return `expect` (`ok` or a refusal code: mismatch, unsupported_version, unsupported_alg, bad_ttl, expired, clock_skew, bad_token, unknown_key, not_trusted, bad_sig). Check order: field mismatch (including proposal.target_id == record.target_id and the recomputed req_sha256), version, alg, safe integers (sig.ts_ms, sig.exp_ms and record.exp_ms must be <= 2^53-1, else bad_token), ttl (0 < exp_ms - issued_ms <= 5 min), expiry, skew (issued_ms and ts_ms within 5 min of now_ms), tokens (fps are 64 lowercase hex, target_id mx_[0-9a-f]+, nonce 32 lowercase hex, other ids tokens [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}, proposal valid), key, trust, signature. ts_ms is only bound by the 5 minute skew around now_ms, not by the challenge window (see ok_ts_in_future_exactly_5_min). After a successful verify the caller checks the spawn prompt bytes against proposal.prompt_sha256: equal SHA-256, or both absent; anything else is mismatch. `wire_json_cases[]`: the raw wire JSON text must be accepted (`ok`) or refused (`refused`) by the parser: unknown fields, duplicate keys, non-integer numbers (a text with '.' or exponent, even 1.0), negative numbers (including -0), and ts_ms/exp_ms above 2^53-1 are refused; a port must inspect raw number tokens because JSON.parse loses the difference. STATEMENT: `statement_cases[]`: a tmgr-spawn-key:v1 statement must carry two valid signatures (device chat sign key `sig`, spawn key `spawn_sig`), and the device must be trusted; `device_kex_pub_b64` is the device kex key used for that case (it feeds the device_fp). Check order: size (<= 512 bytes), prefix and field split (exactly five ':'-separated fields after the prefix, tokens, issued_at_ms canonical decimal <= 2^53-1), base64 of spawn_pub (strict), mismatch (user, device_id, device_fp recomputed from the sign and kex keys), clock_skew (issued_at_ms not more than 5 min after now_ms), key (spawn, sign and kex keys each 65-byte uncompressed on-curve, kex strict base64, spawn key must differ from both the sign key and the kex key, else unknown_key), trust, signatures (device sig first, then spawn sig). `expect` as above. SUPERSEDES: `supersedes_cases[]`: a new statement supersedes the stored one only when same user and device_fp and issued_at_ms is strictly greater. With an equal issued_at_ms and a different key supersedes is false and the caller must REFUSE the new statement; a byte-identical statement is a no-op. KEYBOOK: `keybook_cases[]` replay ops on one empty in-memory key book: `offer` at `now_ms` (expect added, replaced, unchanged, stale, conflict or full (a book holds at most 64 devices; a new device_fp beyond that is full); a first key or a strictly newer statement for the same user and device_fp becomes pending and drops any older entry including its approval; any replacement, approved or pending, records now_ms; identical is unchanged; older is stale; equal issued_at_ms with another key, or another user for the same device_fp, is conflict), `approve` by device_fp prefix plus the first `fingerprint_prefix_len` chars of `spawn_fingerprint` as the spawn-key prefix, at `now_ms` (fp prefix at least 8 chars and the spawn-key prefix at least 16 chars (64 bits; the full 64 is accepted) else prefix_too_short; device_fp prefix must match exactly one pending entry: none is not_found, several is ambiguous; the spawn-key prefix must be a prefix of lowercase-hex sha256 of that entry's spawn_pub bytes else key_mismatch; an entry replaced less than 60000 ms before now_ms is too_soon; a replacement time later than now_ms is clamped to now_ms), The owner must type the spawn-key fingerprint shown on the PHONE (lowercase hex SHA-256 of the 65 uncompressed spawn-key bytes), never copy it from the machine's pending list, because the check exists to compare what the phone shows with what this machine holds. `pinned_key` (a key only for an approved entry of that user; pending keys are never pinned and must never reach verify).
